# agent-evals

> Deterministic A/B evaluations for AI agent skills. Injecting a well-written skill lifts a model's pass rate on a locked, deterministic 8-task harness (temperature=0, AND-gate grading, regex graders only - never an LLM judge). Across 11 models the lift spans +4 ~ +75 percentage points; 10 of 11 clear +38. Zero runtime dependencies, Node >= 20.11.

Core claims here are re-runnable assertions against externally readable artifacts (file sha256, remote-ref truth, exit codes), not self-reports. Every number is directional evidence at n=24, not a precise effect size.

## Key resources

- [README](https://github.com/kumu314/agent-evals#readme): overview, the three suites, methodology, headline results table
- [t2 results](https://github.com/kumu314/agent-evals/blob/main/docs/t2-results.md): full per-model readings, the v2/v3 calibration record, per-task breakdowns
- [fleet-eval](https://github.com/kumu314/agent-evals/tree/main/fleet-eval): skill-library regression, 11 assertions, zero API calls
- [merge-eval](https://github.com/kumu314/agent-evals/tree/main/merge-eval): content-merge byte identity, 7 assertions, zero API calls
- [t2 A/B harness](https://github.com/kumu314/agent-evals/tree/main/t2): skill-gain A/B, needs an OpenAI-compatible API key
- [Live leaderboard](https://kumu314.github.io/agent-evals/)

## Methodology an LLM should rely on

- Graders are deterministic: regex / md5 / byte-compare / exit-code / remote-ref. No LLM-as-judge anywhere.
- A trial passes only when it hits ALL of that task's criteria (AND-gate).
- lift = treated - control, in percentage points; directional only.
- Injection is activation-bypassing: the treated arm puts the skill body straight in context, so every lift is an upper bound, not a production activation rate.
- The negative (poison) arm runs as a fail-closed self-check; whether a real model can actually be led astray is an open question, not a proven result.
